records.Concise description: BIP 353 standard for publishing human-readable Bitcoin payment instructions in DNS so wallets can resolve names into signed `bitcoin:` payment data.
records.Deeper researched summary: BIP 353 uses DNS TXT records with DNSSEC validation to associate human-readable names with Bitcoin payment instructions, typically a `bitcoin:` URI that can itself reference current payment methods. It is distinct from Lightning Address: both improve names, but BIP 353 uses DNSSEC-authenticated Bitcoin payment instructions rather than LNURL's web-service payRequest flow. Client security depends on correct DNSSEC validation.
records.Launch / history: Standardized in the mid-2020s as a Bitcoin-native human-readable payment-instruction discovery mechanism.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It bridges human naming and multi-method Bitcoin payment instructions while reducing reliance on a single web API convention.
Important technical or cultural characte: DNSSEC validation required by the specification
Can point toward on-chain/Lightning-compatible instructions through the URI layer
records.Verification basis: Primary BIP specification verifies the current standard and its DNSSEC/payment-instruction architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not equate BIP status with universal wallet support.
Wallet implementations must perform the security validation required by the specification; public copy should not suggest plain unauthenticated DNS lookups are equivalent.
Keep distinct from Lightning Address despite similar human-readable goals.

records.Concise description: Deprecated Bitcoin merchant payment protocol that used signed payment requests and merchant-server interactions before ecosystem migration toward simpler URI/invoice approaches.
records.Deeper researched summary: BIP70 Payment Protocol added richer merchant payment requests, certificates/identities and payment acknowledgements beyond a simple Bitcoin URI. It became associated with large payment processors and wallets but accumulated interoperability, dependency and security concerns. Bitcoin Core removed BIP70 support by the 0.20 era; it remains historically useful for understanding why modern Bitcoin payments generally rely on BIP21/321, Lightning invoices and application-level protocols instead.
records.Launch / history: Introduced in 2013-era Bitcoin merchant infrastructure; broadly deprecated in later years and removed from Bitcoin Core by version 0.20.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It materially explains an important abandoned branch of Bitcoin merchant UX and the ecosystem's later preference for simpler, more composable payment instructions.
Important technical or cultural characte: Deprecated and removed from Bitcoin Core
records.Verification basis: Primary BIP history plus Bitcoin Core release documentation supports historical/deprecated classification and removal from Bitcoin Core.
Research notes / uncertainties: Historical does not mean every third-party implementation vanished on the same date; it means BIP70 is a legacy payment approach rather than a current canonical direction.
Do not use old BitPay/BIP70 behavior to describe BitPay's current payment flow.

records.Concise description: Open Chaumian ecash protocol in which mints issue blinded bearer tokens representing satoshi-denominated claims, often funded and redeemed through Lightning.
records.Deeper researched summary: Cashu is a Bitcoin-oriented ecash protocol, not an on-chain token system. A Cashu mint operates Lightning/payment infrastructure and custodies the bitcoin backing its issued ecash; users hold bearer ecash tokens and trust the mint to honor redemption even though blind signatures improve the mint's transactional privacy visibility. Cashu wallets therefore are not themselves Lightning wallets merely because mints commonly bridge deposits and withdrawals over Lightning.
Creators / founders: Calle — original protocol creator; open-source contributors
records.Launch / history: Developed in the early 2020s as a modern Chaumian ecash protocol designed for Bitcoin/Lightning ecosystems and evolved through the NUT specification set.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It expands the payment design space beyond channels and on-chain transactions while making a very different trust tradeoff explicit: private bearer payments inside a mint domain in exchange for mint custody of backing bitcoin.
Important technical or cultural characte: Mint-issued bearer tokens denominated in sats
Lightning commonly used for mint ingress/egress
Ecash tokens are not on-chain bitcoin
records.Verification basis: Current official Cashu documentation and protocol specifications explicitly describe the mint custody model, bearer ecash tokens and Lightning relationship.
Research notes / uncertainties: Never describe Cashu tokens as on-chain bitcoin or as Bitcoin consensus assets.
Do not call Cashu globally non-custodial: the mint has custody of backing bitcoin.
Fedimint is related but excluded from PAYMENTS canonical inventory because its broader federated protocol/application framework belongs more naturally under NETWORK.
